A caution: some paper titles and authors suggested in our earlier chat may not match real publications, so please check them on Google Scholar. The works below are well-established.

## Recommendations

### Upcoming conferences in medical imaging (as of May 2023)
- **MICCAI 2023** (Vancouver, October 8–12): This is the top venue for your topics. Its workshops cover domain adaptation (DART), interpretability (iMIMIC) and multimodal learning.
- **MIDL 2023** (Medical Imaging with Deep Learning, July): A smaller conference with strong deep learning content and open-review papers.
- **IPMI 2023** (June): A highly selective conference focused on methods.
- **ISBI** and **SPIE Medical Imaging**: Good for applied work.
- **CVPR 2023** (Vancouver, June): Has medical computer vision workshops. The **ML4H workshop at NeurIPS** is also worth following.

### Journals to follow
- *Medical Image Analysis*
- *IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging*
- *Radiology: Artificial Intelligence*
- *Nature Machine Intelligence*

### Recent publications worth reading
- **nnU-Net** (Isensee et al., *Nature Methods*, 2021): A self-configuring segmentation baseline.
- **TransUNet** (Chen et al., 2021) and **Swin-UNETR** (Hatamizadeh et al., 2022): Transformers applied to medical segmentation.
- **Segment Anything** (Kirillov et al., April 2023) and its new medical adaptations, such as **MedSAM**: Foundation models are the hottest topic right now.
- **ConVIRT** (Zhang et al.), **GLoRIA** (Huang et al., 2021) and **BiomedCLIP** (2023): Multi-modal image-text learning, which connects to your fusion and transfer learning interests.
- **Med-PaLM** (Google, 2022–23): Large models for medicine.
- **MONAI**: An open-source PyTorch framework for medical imaging that is handy for reproducing papers.

- **Conferences:** AAMAS (multi-agent systems), CoRL (robot learning), and the main machine learning venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR).
- **Climate Change AI** workshops held at NeurIPS and ICLR.

### Step 2: Recommend publications and conferences
Using **May 30, 2023** as the reference date in your question, these are particularly relevant recent publications:

| Publication | Why you might find it interesting |
|---|---|
| **“A Generalist Agent” — Reed et al. (2022)** | Introduces Gato, a model spanning language, vision, games, and robot control—a strong match for your interest in multimodal agents. |
| **“RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale” — Brohan et al. (2022)** | Explores language-conditioned robot control learned from large-scale real-world demonstrations. |
| **“Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances” — Ahn et al. (2022)** | Connects language-model planning with executable robotic skills; useful for agents that translate instructions into actions. |
| **“The Surprising Effectiveness of PPO in Cooperative Multi-Agent Games” — Yu et al. (NeurIPS 2022)** | A valuable empirical study and baseline for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning. |
| **“Towards General Purpose Vision Foundation Models for Medical Image Analysis: An Experimental Study of DINOv2 on Radiology Benchmarks” — 2023 preprint** | Examines transferring general-purpose visual representations to medical imaging, directly matching your transfer-learning interests. |
| **“Segment Anything” — Kirillov et al. (April 2023 preprint)** | Introduces promptable segmentation. Although not medical-specific, it raises useful research questions about adapting segmentation foundation models to clinical images. |

**Conferences to follow:**
- **ICML 2023, July 23–29, Honolulu:** Especially relevant for reinforcement learning, multimodal learning, and adaptation.
- **AAMAS 2023, May 29–June 2, London:** The most directly aligned venue for your multi-agent interests.
- **ICRA 2023, May 29–June 2, London:** Strong coverage of robotics, autonomous systems, and robot learning.
- **CVPR 2023, June 18–22, Vancouver:** Useful for multimodal vision, segmentation, and visual representations.
- **MICCAI 2023, October 8–12, Vancouver:** Your strongest specialist match for medical image analysis.
- **CoRL 2023, November 6–9, Atlanta:** Particularly relevant at the intersection of robotics and reinforcement learning.
- **NeurIPS 2023, December 10–16, New Orleans:** Broad coverage of your AI interests; also look for **Climate Change AI** workshops and related sustainability work.

**My suggested starting point:** Read **Gato**, **RT-1**, and the **MAPPO paper**, then follow **AAMAS/CoRL** for agent research and **MICCAI** for medical imaging. These offer the closest fit to your stated projects and research goals.
